A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TopER research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TopER classification, clustering, runtime and filtration-ablation results, including OGBG-MOLHIV experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds sensitivity studies, timing comparisons, filtration-substitution experiments and synthetic graph visualizations.

M1.justification: The filtration-to-node/edge-count regression, popularity function, point refinement and classifiers remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 adds an evaluated variant replacing Ollivier-Ricci filtration with heat kernel signatures (HKS). Although v1 mentions HKS among possible filtration functions, it does not report this concrete substitution.

E1.justification: The nine real-world benchmark datasets and synthetic power-law runtime scenario are retained. Appendix D adds Erdős–Rényi synthetic graph visualization experiments, extending the represented graph families without changing the main benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds comparison rows for DiffPool, P-WL-C, SAGPool, Top-k, 1-GIN (GFL), MinCutPool, RePHINE and GPSE. DiffPool previously appeared only within the aggregated six-GNN comparison. These literature-sourced results substantially broaden the explicit comparator set; Appendix D also compares TopER visualizations with PCA-projected PH embeddings.

E3.justification: The existing stratified ten-fold classification setup and classifier hyperparameters are retained. Added evaluation designs include matched sublevel-degree TopER/PH timing with Betti vectorization, threshold sweeps from 10 to 500, one-to-four filtration combinations, HKS substitution, and synthetic PH/PCA visualization with 50 thresholds. These substantially expand the experimental controls and configurations rather than establish reruns of the original benchmarks.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained individual-function ablation and MOLHIV function-addition study, v3 adds threshold sensitivity, incremental filtration combinations across eight datasets, Ollivier-Ricci removal and HKS replacement, and per-filtration timing analyses (Appendix A). Table 15 quantifies quadratic-fit coefficients, while Appendix D adds synthetic visualization comparisons.

E5.justification: v1 reports plus/minus values without explicitly defining their statistical meaning. v3 identifies mean ± standard deviation across multiple runs in Appendix A.6/Table 13 and makes a broader disclosure in its checklist. Neither a repeated-run count nor an increase in runs is established; ten-fold cross-validation and the MOLHIV seed of 16 are retained.

E6.justification: Headline TopER classification, MOLHIV and clustering scores remain unchanged, but numerous baseline, ablation, timing and synthetic results are added. New Table 8 reports REDDIT-B accuracy of 79.55±2.20 for TopER-1 versus 84.50±2.51 for PH, with runtimes of 107.65 versus 9173.37 seconds. Reported MOLHIV runtime changes from 16.5 to 7.85 hours and REDDIT-5K filtration computation from 34.6 to 2.91 hours; the PDFs do not explain these revisions sufficiently to establish a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: The stability statements and Appendix C proofs are substantively retained; reproducing existing lemmas in the main text adds no new theorem. Remark 3.3 adds an algebraic connection to Euler characteristic. Its proposed equivalence contains a sign inconsistency: it identifies y_i−x_i with χ after defining χ=x_i−y_i.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about efficient, interpretable embeddings and competitive performance. The introduction replaces the contribution claiming enhanced use and improved performance of traditional PH with an explicit topology-inspired design that avoids persistence diagrams and Betti-number computation. This refines the claimed contribution without replacing the paper's central thesis.

C2.justification: v3 explains filtration combinations as complementary structural perspectives and discusses when interpretability may outweigh predictive performance. It adds an explicit limitation concerning filtration choice and required domain knowledge, plus interpretations of threshold robustness and HKS substitution. Existing pivot/growth interpretations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 discloses selected embedding dimensions of 14–26 in Table 14, adds per-filtration runtime information, and replaces the anonymous code pointer with a named GitHub repository. Conversely, it removes the MOLHIV table's sublevel/superlevel column and the explicit Lasso cv=10 setting. These are documentation and access-information changes; retained classifier hyperparameters do not establish a configuration revision.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss aggregation and hierarchical pooling, with references including DiffPool, SAGPool, Top-k and MinCutPool. v3 also explicitly positions its direct interpretable embeddings against GPSE and GFSE and adds relevant filtration-learning and HKS references. The broader research positioning remains intact; updated publication metadata for existing references is not new literature.

P1.justification: Most existing technical and results prose is retained. Local restructuring nests related work within Background, integrates ablations into classification results, reorders appendix material and relocates the algorithm. Contributions and selected explanations are rewritten, with new limitations, acknowledgments, checklist and broader-impact sections; this is an extension and localized reorganization rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds six analytical tables and three multipanel synthetic visualization figures, expands Table 2, and changes the columns of the hyperparameter and MOLHIV tables. Algorithm 1 and the retained scalability plot move to the appendix, while several existing displays are resized or repositioned. The conference template, title block and table presentation also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons and new controlled timing, threshold and filtration studies make the empirical support more informative, particularly about accuracy–cost tradeoffs. These gains are tempered by lost MOLHIV filtration details, the new Euler-characteristic sign inconsistency, and a PH-runtime claim naming REDDIT-5K although Table 8 evaluates REDDIT-B. The revision provides a limited net quality improvement without resolving the existing disconnect between the Betti-pair stability analysis and the implemented node/edge-count representation.
